newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Fujimori seeks micro-financing to fight poverty.
newsitem.headline: Fujimori seeks micro-financing to fight poverty.

text.p: Peruvian President Alberto Fujimori said on Sunday that his country would try to introduce the Bangladeshi model of micro-financing to fight poverty.
"We want to introduce this kind of tool to fight poverty," Fujimori told a news conference at the end of his formal talks with Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina.
Fujimori, who arrived here on Saturday, visited Bangladeshi non-governmental organisations (NGOs) offering small credit to millions of poor Bangladeshis.

On Saturday he visited the Dhaka central office of the Bangladesh Rural Advancement Committee (BRAC), one of country's NGOs helping the rural poor, especially women, with small income generating loans.

Fujimori's visit, first to Bangladesh by a head of a South American nation, was prompted by the outcome of micro-credit summit held in Washington last December year when foreign leaders praised Bangladesh's efforts for fighting poverty by providing small credit to the rural poor.
Fujimori said: "We will interchange some of our experience...in micro financing."
He said Peru wanted to bolster trade and economic relations with Bangladesh. "There is a big potential for increasing trade," he said.
Fujimori's visit triggered street protests on Friday and Saturday by left-wing groups and students which denounced the Peruvian government's actions against communist workers.
During the talks between Fujimori and Hasina, Bangladesh offered skilled agricultural and industrial labourers, the Foreign Ministry said.

"Our Prime Minister lauded Peru's rapid development and said she would be happy if Peru ever required our manpower in its agriculture, industry and service sectors," Foreign Secretary Farooq Sobhan told reporters after the talks.
"Peru is growing very fast, they might need overseas workers in future," he said.
"Our ties are now at nascent stage but there is ample scope for boosting economic relations especially when Lima is keen for developing ties with the South Asian region," said Sobhan.
Annual trade between Lima and Dhaka accounts for less than $1 million.
